explain.ja: 駒の並べ方の作法には大橋流と伊藤流があります。大橋流はプロ棋士の約8割が使う方法で、まず王将を置き、王将に近い順に左金・右金・左銀・右銀と左右対称に並べ、9段目が終わったら8段目、7段目と進めます。伊藤流は途中まで大橋流と同じですが、歩を左から順に並べ、飛車・角・香車を最後に置くのが特徴です。これは敵陣に飛車・角・香車が向かないようにする配慮だとされます。必ずしも守る必要はありません。
explain.en: There are two main etiquette orders for setting up: Ohashi and Ito. Ohashi, used by about 80% of professionals, places the king first, then left gold, right gold, left silver, right silver symmetrically outward from the king, finishing the ninth rank before the eighth and seventh. Ito is the same up to a point but places pawns from the left in order and puts the rook, bishop and lances last, reportedly so that these pieces do not face the opponent's camp while being set. None of this is mandatory.

section.ja: 将棋の駒の並べ方は?飛車と角の位置に注意!
section.en: How to set up the shogi pieces? Watch the rook and bishop positions!

title.ja: 大橋流の並べる順番（数字は並べる手順）
title.en: Ohashi-style setup order (numbers show the order of placement)

explain.ja: NHK杯などのテレビ対局では、プロ棋士が大橋流で並べているのが見られます。伊藤流は途中まで大橋流と同じで、香車を並べないまま進めます。次に歩を左から順に並べ、最後に左香、右香、角、飛車の順で置きます。
explain.en: On TV games such as the NHK Cup you can see professionals set up in the Ohashi style. The Ito style matches Ohashi up to a point but leaves the lances out first, then places the pawns from the left, and finally the left lance, right lance, bishop and rook in that order.

title.ja: 伊藤流の並べる順番（数字は並べる手順）
title.en: Ito-style setup order (numbers show the order of placement)

explain.ja: 初期配置は、先手側から見て一段目に香桂銀金玉金銀桂香、二段目に飛と角、三段目に歩、七段目に歩、八段目に角と飛、九段目に香桂銀金玉金銀桂香が並びます。先手も後手も同じ配置で、飛車が右側(2筋)、角が左側(8筋)になるので間違えないよう注意しましょう。大橋流は中央から左右対称に並べ、伊藤流は歩を左から並べて飛車・角・香車を最後にするので、相手に駒を向けない敬意を表す並べ方です。対局では上手が先に並べ始め、上手が王将、下手が玉将を持つのが正式なマナーで、駒は丁寧に置きます。普段の対局ではそこまで気にしなくて構いません。
explain.en: The initial setup, from the side of the player nearest you, is lance-knight-silver-gold-king-gold-silver-knight-lance on the back rank, the bishop and rook on the next rank, and a full rank of pawns on the third; the other side mirrors it. The rook goes on the right (file 2) and the bishop on the left (file 8), a common mistake point. Ohashi places pieces symmetrically from the centre, while Ito places pawns from the left and leaves rook, bishop and lances for last, as a courtesy so they do not face the opponent. By etiquette the stronger player (上手) starts setting up and takes the 王将, the weaker takes the 玉将, and pieces are placed gently. In casual games this need not be strict.

title.ja: 駒台への持ち駒の並べ方：種類ごとにまとめて置く
title.en: Arranging pieces on the komadai: group them by type

explain.ja: 持ち駒は相手にも見えるように置かなければなりません。並べる順番を間違えても反則ではなく、最終的に正しい初期配置になっていれば問題ありません。王将と玉将の動きも強さも同じで、上手が王将を持つのは慣習にすぎません。まずは並べ順より完成形の初期配置を覚えることを優先しましょう。
explain.en: Pieces in hand must be displayed so the opponent can see them. Setting up in the wrong order is not a violation as long as the final starting position is correct. The 王将 and 玉将 are identical in movement and strength, and the stronger player taking 王将 is only a custom. Beginners should prioritise memorising the finished setup over the order.
